subject: Reliable contradictions should take priority over counts of supporting observations when comparing explanations.
rationale: This comparative priority faithfully implements the source's emphasis on inconsistency and diagnostic importance rather than simple supporting counts. It is relevant to distinguishing the target's multiple plausible causes despite incomplete and differing measurements. Within this methodological scope, no numerical weighting rule is required; reliability, diagnosticity and sensitivity still govern interpretation. This licenses the proposed comparison without establishing that any contradiction or causal finding has been observed.
